patch.value: Promotion budget reservation is a read-then-write race, so concurrent promotions can exceed the approved budget

CodeRabbit review of pm-rl#12, Critical. promoteGeneration counts promotions already made under an approval item and then writes its own promotion. Two concurrent promotions both read the count, both observe headroom, and both proceed.

Why this is the most serious defect in the module: the approved budget exists so a RECURSIVE loop cannot advance past the point a human authorized, and a recursive loop is precisely the caller that promotes programmatically rather than by hand. The guarantee fails in its own primary scenario.

Needs an atomic reservation, and an adversarial test that issues concurrent promotions and asserts the permitted count is never exceeded.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: promoteGeneration now wraps countPromotedUnderApproval + the promotion write in client.claim(approvalId), released in a finally. A lost test-and-set race -> budget_contended (CONFLICT) naming the approval item, telling the caller to retry, never falling through. Non-race claim failures (e.g. terminal approval) rethrow as-is. isAlreadyClaimedError is not a public SDK export in this version; the race is detected structurally via context.code === 'already_claimed_by' (the exact predicate the SDK helper applies). Empirical scratch-script observation on a real Decision item: claim sets assignee to the author WITHOUT changing status (open->open); release restores assignee to undefined and leaves status unchanged, so release fully restores the prior state and no explicit restore is needed. Adversarial test: Promise.allSettled over 6 real PmClients (distinct authors) promoting 6 distinct candidates against a budget of 1 asserts exactly one succeeds. Revert-proof: reverting the claim wrapper lets 4 succeed (>1) and is restored.

author=harness:claude-code,text=Reimplemented on the SDK's commitWorkspaceTransaction instead of the claim-as-mutex this item was first fixed with. The claim version did serialize, but a loser was refused with budget_contended, a RETRYABLE message for a PERMANENT state. A recursive loop, the exact caller this budget exists to bound, would retry that forever instead of stopping. Under the writer lock the second caller instead waits, re-reads the count the winner just changed, and gets the accurate terminal budget_exceeded.

It also removes the reimplemented SDK predicate: isAlreadyClaimedError is declared in the typings but exported from no public subpath, so the claim version had to hard-code the already_claimed_by context code. Filed upstream as pm-cli issue 975. The transaction needs no error predicate at all.

Verified rather than assumed, in this order:
- Mutual exclusion across OS PROCESSES, proven before writing the fix: two processes in a transaction step each appending ENTER, sleeping 1200ms, then EXIT produced ENTER A, EXIT A, ENTER B, EXIT B.
- The adversarial test is revert-proof: bypassing the lock lets 3 of 6 concurrent promotions succeed against a budget of 1. With the lock, exactly 1 succeeds and the other 5 report budget_exceeded, asserted with doesNotMatch against any contention wording.
- compensate is NOT called when apply throws, probed empirically: the sequence is inspect, inspect, apply, then the error propagates. So the revert is invoked by apply itself on a failed close, and the same function is wired as compensate. A test with a real client whose close throws proves the body is reverted, the item stays open, and the unspent budget is still available.
- The promoted count now EXCLUDES the generation being promoted, which is what makes it correct when its own write is already present.

Removed an unreachable inspect branch rather than papering over it: reporting a durable applied state is impossible to reach because the already_promoted guard fires before the transaction opens, and the journal alone drives replay skipping. Coverage is a genuine 100/100/100 over 126 tests.

patch.value:
Reimplemented on the SDK's commitWorkspaceTransaction instead of the claim-as-mutex this item was first fixed with. The claim version did serialize, but a loser was refused with budget_contended, a RETRYABLE message for a PERMANENT state. A recursive loop, the exact caller this budget exists to bound, would retry that forever instead of stopping. Under the writer lock the second caller instead waits, re-reads the count the winner just changed, and gets the accurate terminal budget_exceeded.

It also removes a reimplemented SDK predicate: isAlreadyClaimedError is declared in the typings but exported from no public subpath, so the claim version had to hard-code the already_claimed_by context code. Filed upstream as pm-cli issue 975. The transaction needs no error predicate at all.

A later review round then found the fix was still incomplete, and the follow-up was more serious than the finding that led to it. The already_promoted check ran BEFORE the lock, on a read every concurrent caller performs before any of them holds it, so three concurrent promotions of the SAME generation all passed it and all succeeded. Re-checking inside the critical section makes "a generation promotes at most once" true under concurrency. Keying transactionId on the generation ALSO had to go: it made concurrent callers look like replays of one committed transaction, so the journal skipped apply and every caller reported success for a promotion only one of them performed. The transaction is used here for mutual exclusion, not idempotent replay, and the two must not share a key.

Verified rather than assumed, in this order:
- Mutual exclusion across OS PROCESSES, proven before writing the fix: two processes in a transaction step each appending ENTER, sleeping 1200ms, then EXIT produced ENTER A, EXIT A, ENTER B, EXIT B.
- Budget adversarial test is revert-proof: bypassing the lock lets 3 of 6 concurrent promotions succeed against a budget of 1. With it, exactly 1 succeeds and the other 5 report budget_exceeded, asserted with doesNotMatch against any contention wording.
- Same-generation adversarial test is revert-proof: removing the in-lock re-check makes 3 of 3 concurrent promotions of one generation succeed.
- compensate is NOT called when apply throws, probed empirically: inspect, inspect, apply, then the error propagates. So the revert is invoked by apply itself on a failed close, and the same function is wired as compensate.

An earlier excludeId guard on the promoted count was REMOVED rather than kept: a reviewer showed the test naming it stayed green when the guard was deleted, and once the promoted re-check moved inside the lock the guard was both unnecessary and unreachable.

value.text: A third stale record on this item cannot be corrected through the CLI and is left in place deliberately. The linked test entry named promotion rethrows a non-race claim failure on the approval item records result=pass for a test that was deleted along with the claim mutex it covered. pm test --remove cannot select it: the stored command contains a comma and an equals sign, which are the selector's own pair delimiters, so every removal form returns ok:true and removes nothing. Hand-editing the toon would break the history chain that pm health verifies. Filed upstream as pm-cli#982, which also asks that a removal matching nothing stop reporting success.
